reason: It is one developer, version 0.4.1, and the page says nothing about source code, code signing or independent reviews, so I will not run an unknown .exe on my PC. My current viewer already opens my phone photos instantly.
why_switch_or_not: The speed numbers are from the developer's own PC and benchmark, so I can't treat them as proof, and my viewer is already fast enough for relatives' phone photos. RAW, PSD, 3D, video and an editor are things I never use. I would also want to know the colour management won't change how my photos look when I print one, and the page only says 'colour management with ICC profiles' with no detail.
current_app_pros: Small, starts instantly, next/back is quick, opens JPG/PNG/WebP/HEIC-type phone photos and screenshots without fuss, no installer baggage, and I know how it behaves.
current_app_pains: Nothing much. Occasionally the print dialog is clumsy and I can't open a PDF in it, but I just use another program for that.
objection: I don't know who this person is or whether the exe is safe. No source, no signature, no reviews, only one developer's own benchmark. Why would I put that on my PC when my current viewer already works?
would_change_my_mind: Open source code or a code-signed installer, plus a few independent reviews or a recommendation from a site or person I trust, and a clear statement that it won't change my photos' colours when printing.
